questions.question: Why must a permutation matrix be square?
options: Only square matrices can have exactly one $1$ in each row.
It must equal its own transpose, which only square matrices can do.
It is a diagonal matrix, and diagonal matrices are square.
It represents a rearrangement of the same number of coordinates.

questions.question: Why is the identity matrix a permutation matrix?
options: One $1$ in each row and each column.
It swaps every pair of rows.
It has determinant zero.
It has all entries equal to $1$.

questions.question: How many entries equal to $1$ does a $4\times4$ permutation matrix have?
Is $\begin{pmatrix}1&0&0\\0&0&1\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$ a permutation matrix?
options: No, because the ones are not all on the main diagonal.
No, because it is $3\times3$.
Yes, each row and each column has exactly one $1$.
No, because it has zeros.

questions.question: Why is the product of two permutation matrices again a permutation matrix?
options: Products of $0$-$1$ matrices are always $0$-$1$ matrices.
Each product has exactly $n$ ones, which is all that is needed.
Doing two reorderings in succession is still a reordering.
Permutation matrices are symmetric, so the product is too.

questions.question: Compute $\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix}\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\5&7\end{pmatrix}$.
options: $\begin{pmatrix}0&0\\0&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}2&3\\5&7\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}5&7\\2&3\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}3&2\\7&5\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: A student says any $0$-$1$ square matrix with exactly $n$ ones is a permutation matrix. What is missing?
options: The ones must be distributed one per row and one per column.
The ones must all lie on the main diagonal or the anti-diagonal.
The matrix must also be symmetric, with $P=P^{\top}$.
The matrix must also have determinant $1$ rather than $-1$.

questions.question: Let $P=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$. What is $P\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}$?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}y\\z\\x\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}x\\z\\y\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}x+y+z\\x+y+z\\x+y+z\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}z\\x\\y\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: Let $\boldsymbol{P}=\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$. Which matrix is $\boldsymbol{P}^{-1}$?
options: $\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\0&0&1\\1&0&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&0&1\\1&0&0\\0&1&0\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&1&0\\1&0&0\\0&0&1\end{pmatrix}$
$\begin{pmatrix}0&0&-1\\-1&0&0\\0&-1&0\end{pmatrix}$

questions.question: In an LU decomposition with row swaps, written $\boldsymbol{P}\boldsymbol{A}=\boldsymbol{L}\boldsymbol{U}$, what does the permutation matrix $\boldsymbol{P}$ do?
options: It applies the row interchanges to the rows of $\boldsymbol{A}$.
It stores the elimination multipliers below the diagonal.
It scales the rows of $\boldsymbol{A}$ so that every pivot is $1$.
It reorders the columns of $\boldsymbol{A}$ before elimination.
